review_locator: Beyond the Matrix: The Many Non-ECM Ligands for Integrins, PMCID:PMC5855671; Reactome R-HSA-202706
primary_title: JAM2 interacts with alpha4beta1. Facilitation by JAM3; Junctional adhesion molecule (JAM)-B supports lymphocyte rolling and adhesion through interaction with alpha4beta1 integrin
decision_basis: The integrin review identifies JAM-B/JAM2 as an alpha4beta1 counter-receptor; the cited primary studies show JAM2-alpha4beta1 interaction and alpha4beta1-dependent T-cell rolling and sticking, with prior JAM3 engagement required.
limitations_preserved: Retain JAM3-facilitated heterotypic membrane topology and human T-cell rolling/sticking context; no standalone JAM2 relay or SCI inference.

review_locator: Beyond the Matrix: The Many Non-ECM Ligands for Integrins, PMCID:PMC5855671
primary_title: Integrin alphaVbeta3 contains a cell surface receptor site for thyroid hormone that is linked to activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase and induction of angiogenesis
decision_basis: The integrin review cites the primary study identifying a cell-surface T4 receptor site on alphaVbeta3; radioligand binding and integrin blockade/knockdown link T4 to MAPK activation and proangiogenic function.
limitations_preserved: Restrict to non-genomic T4 binding/signaling at alphaVbeta3 in the tested CV-1 context; do not generalize to T3, nuclear thyroid receptors, or SCI.

review_locator: Beyond the Matrix: The Many Non-ECM Ligands for Integrins, PMCID:PMC5855671
primary_title: Integrin alphaVbeta3 contains a receptor site for resveratrol; alphavbeta3 Integrin-dependent antiangiogenic activity of resveratrol stereoisomers
decision_basis: The integrin review cites primary binding and endothelial-function studies showing trans-resveratrol interacts with the beta3-containing alphaVbeta3 receptor near the RGD pocket, activates ERK/p53-linked apoptosis, and inhibits alphaVbeta3-dependent endothelial angiogenic behavior.
limitations_preserved: Restrict to trans-resveratrol and alphaVbeta3 receptor/function; cis-resveratrol is weaker in the angiogenesis study, and no SCI inference is added.
